facts.fact: The Presidency's release says the unique-identifier enrolment, launched 11 November 2026, is run by the ministry in charge of digital transition, with everything done by Burkinabè engineers and Burkina's public bodies.
President Traoré says the identifier system is purely Burkinabè, made by Burkinabè engineers and public bodies, with data hosting centres in Burkina Faso.

systems.owner: Ministry in charge of digital transition

BFA.note: Who maintains the system after launch is not stated.
The identifier is said to be a common reference for public files, but no register is stated to use it yet.

facts.fact: On 11 November 2026 President Traoré launched mass enrolment in the register of the electronic unique identifier, issuing a free random 12-digit number per person, through 160 enrolment sites and mobile teams.
The Presidency's release says enrolment collects photograph, fingerprints and iris data to eliminate multiple records, so each person holds a single number.

systems.owner: Ministry in charge of digital transition

BFA.note: No certification, audit or assurance level stated, and no population share enrolled.

facts.fact: President Traoré says the identifier system's data is hosted in data centres in Burkina Faso, which he calls purely Burkinabè and run by Burkinabè public structures.
